subject: en_read
source: English National Curriculum — English programmes of study: key stage 2 (Year 6), reading comprehension, DfE 2013; KS2 English reading test framework (STA)

weeks.topic: Classic adventure: Treasure Island
objectives: Read an extract from a classic adventure
Work out archaic vocabulary from context
Discuss how the author builds suspense

weeks.topic: WWII historical fiction: character development
objectives: Track how a character develops through a story
Infer feelings from evidence
Discuss the impact of the historical setting

weeks.topic: First World War poetry: tone and mood
objectives: Identify the tone and mood of war poems
Explore how language creates emotion
Compare the views of different poets

weeks.topic: Primary sources: wartime letters and diaries
objectives: Read primary sources from wartime
Distinguish between fact and opinion
Infer what life was like from evidence

weeks.topic: Dystopian fiction: themes of freedom and choice
objectives: Identify the features of dystopian fiction
Discuss themes of freedom and rules
Compare the fictional world with our own

weeks.topic: Shakespeare: Macbeth retold — plot and character
objectives: Follow the plot of a retold Shakespeare play
Infer characters' motives such as ambition
Discuss how Shakespeare creates tension

weeks.topic: Contemporary fiction: empathy and viewpoint
objectives: Read a modern novel about a refugee child (e.g. The Boy at the Back of the Class)
Explore the narrator's viewpoint
Discuss themes of empathy and belonging

weeks.topic: Newspaper articles: bias, fact and opinion
objectives: Compare two articles about the same event
Identify bias in word choice
Distinguish fact from opinion

weeks.topic: Persuasive speeches: rhetorical devices
objectives: Identify rhetorical devices in famous speeches
Explain the effect on the audience
Evaluate how persuasive a speech is

weeks.topic: Norse myths compared with Greek myths
objectives: Read Norse myths (e.g. Thor, Loki)
Compare gods and heroes across mythologies
Identify common themes

weeks.topic: Detective fiction: Sherlock Holmes and deduction
objectives: Follow clues to make deductions
Explain how the author reveals information
Predict the solution with evidence

weeks.topic: Classic poetry: The Listeners
objectives: Explore the atmosphere of a classic poem
Discuss ambiguity and open questions
Analyse the effect of rhythm and sound

weeks.topic: Scientific texts: technical vocabulary
objectives: Read explanation texts linked to science
Work out technical vocabulary
Retrieve and summarise key information

weeks.topic: Book and film: comparing versions of a story
objectives: Compare a book with its film adaptation
Discuss what is changed, added or left out
Explain which version is more effective

weeks.topic: Term 1 review: comparing genres and themes
objectives: Revisit inference and retrieval skills
Compare themes across texts read this term
Answer test-style questions

weeks.topic: Fantasy: The Hobbit — journeys and quests
objectives: Explore the structure of a quest narrative
Track a character's journey and growth
Discuss the language used to describe settings

weeks.topic: Gothic and ghost stories: building atmosphere
objectives: Identify features of gothic writing
Explain how authors build atmosphere
Discuss the use of humour in ghost stories (The Canterville Ghost)

weeks.topic: Biography: inspiring lives (Nelson Mandela)
objectives: Read a biography of an inspiring figure
Summarise key events in chronological order
Discuss qualities and values

weeks.topic: Balanced arguments: evaluating evidence
objectives: Identify arguments and counter-arguments
Evaluate the strength of evidence
Form and justify an opinion

weeks.topic: Poetry: extended metaphor and figurative language
objectives: Identify extended metaphors in poems
Explain how figurative language creates meaning
Compare poems by different poets

weeks.topic: Folk tales from around the world: shared themes
objectives: Read folk tales from different cultures
Identify themes and conventions shared across cultures
Discuss what they teach readers

weeks.topic: Short stories: twist endings and structure
objectives: Analyse the structure of short stories
Identify how authors set up twist endings
Predict endings using clues

weeks.topic: Travel writing: the author's voice
objectives: Identify the author's voice in travel writing
Explore descriptive language about places
Distinguish fact from personal opinion

weeks.topic: Modern classic: Holes — interweaving storylines
objectives: Track interweaving storylines
Explain how events in the past link to the present
Discuss themes of fate and friendship

weeks.topic: Information texts: charts, tables and diagrams
objectives: Interpret information in charts, tables and diagrams
Combine information from text and graphics
Answer retrieval questions accurately

weeks.topic: Playscripts: dialogue, stage directions and performance
objectives: Read a playscript and analyse stage directions
Infer character from dialogue
Perform a scene with expression

weeks.topic: Mock assessment: KS2-style reading paper
objectives: Complete a reading paper under timed conditions
Answer a range of question types
Identify targets for revision

weeks.topic: SATs revision: retrieval and vocabulary questions
objectives: Practise retrieval and find-and-copy questions
Explain word meanings in context
Manage time across a reading paper

weeks.topic: SATs revision: inference and explanation questions
objectives: Practise inference questions with two pieces of evidence
Answer explain and compare questions
Use PEE in longer answers

weeks.topic: Comparing texts across genres on one theme: survival
objectives: Read fiction, poetry and non-fiction on survival
Compare how each text presents the theme
Discuss which text is most powerful

weeks.topic: Humour and wordplay: puns and irony (The Phantom Tollbooth)
objectives: Identify puns, idioms and irony
Explain how wordplay creates humour
Discuss how the author plays with language

weeks.topic: Poetry anthology: choosing and justifying favourites
objectives: Read widely across poetry anthologies
Choose favourite poems and explain why
Recite a poem with expression

weeks.topic: Reading for research: note-making from sources
objectives: Make notes from more than one source
Organise information under headings
Acknowledge sources

weeks.topic: Coming-of-age fiction: change and identity
objectives: Explore how characters grow up and change
Discuss themes of identity and transition
Relate themes to own experiences

weeks.topic: Book club: leading a discussion
objectives: Prepare questions to lead a book discussion
Listen and respond to others' views
Recommend books for Year 7

weeks.topic: End-of-year assessment: reading comprehension
objectives: Answer a range of comprehension questions
Use evidence to support answers
Read across genres

weeks.topic: Year 6 reading review and transition
objectives: Reflect on reading across primary school
Set reading goals for secondary school
Choose summer reading
